# The sensitivity grid — where the answer actually lives

**28 Nov 2026** · extreme scenario only · **BNI now at the adopted 1,324 leavers** · generated by `app/model.js`

Two inputs decide the headline, and neither is a fact. Everything else is small next to them.

| Exposure | Attrition basis | Weighted q | Dismissals 2026-30 | JKP cost | Headcount 2030 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **0.30** (placeholder) | all leavers | 5.68% | **2,206** | Rp 33.0 bn | 191,884 |
| 0.30 | voluntary only | 3.95% | **9,522** | Rp 142.3 bn | 191,884 |
| **0.582** (measured) | all leavers | 5.68% | **27,578** | Rp 412.0 bn | 167,214 |
| 0.582 | voluntary only | 3.95% | **34,679** | Rp 518.1 bn | 167,214 |

**The range is 2,206 to 34,679 dismissals — a factor of 15.7 — from two assumptions.** JKP cost spans
Rp 33 bn to Rp 518 bn.

Three things this grid makes unavoidable:

1. **Headcount 2030 moves only with exposure** (191,884 vs 167,214). Attrition changes nothing about how many
   jobs exist; it changes only whether the reduction is absorbed quietly or paid for.
2. **Attrition moves the bill, not the size.** Same 2030 headcount, 4.6x the JKP cost between bases.
3. **Adopting BNI's 1,324 raised the low case from 602 to 2,206.** Fewer separations means less absorption
   capacity, so more of the same shock becomes a dismissal. A data correction made the model harsher.

**Presentation rule (decided today):** both exposure values and both attrition bases travel, labelled. No
single cell of this grid is "the answer" and the report says so.
